last_assistant_message:
**[Rigby]: Root-caused and fixed. Two distinct bugs were compounding, not one.**

**Bug A — the exception-fallback path.** `boot/workflow.md`'s Session Index step (a personal block — I did not touch it) appends to `memory/sessions/index.json` via a plain read-modify-write, not an atomic temp+rename. A hook read landing mid-write can transiently see a partial file, `json.load()` raises `JSONDecodeError`, and `infer_session_id()` fell straight into its exception-handler fallback, minting a disconnected `session-<timestamp>` id — exactly the format on the orphaned record. Fixed with `hook_utils._read_session_index()`: a 3-attempt/80ms retry on `JSONDecodeError`/`OSError` before giving up. `eval-agent-start.py`'s mirrored copy now calls the same shared helper instead of its own single-shot read.

**Bug B — a real (non-error) race, separate from A.** Even with zero exceptions, `infer_session_id()` reads `index[-1]`, and boot's Session Index step appends a *new* entry partway through step-01. Two `UserPromptSubmit` firings for the same logical boot run — one before that append, one after — can each resolve a genuinely valid but *different* `session_id`, and the old `already_open_for_workflow()` was scoped to `session_id`, so it would miss the earlier record and open a second one. Fixed by rekeying that dedup check to workflow name across all open turn-level records instead of session_id — `workflows/{name}/state.yaml` is singular, so two simultaneously in-progress turn-level records for the same workflow name are never legitimate regardless of what session_id each resolved to.

**Verified, not assumed:** built a sandboxed reproduction of the exact race — two calls to `already_open_for_workflow` with two different, both-valid `session_id` values for the same workflow — confirmed only one record gets created after the fix (ran it, pasted the output above: `total records created: 1`).

**Added one more thing beyond what was asked**, flagging it as a deliberate addition: a self-heal sweep in `eval-turn-stop.py`'s `Stop` handler that closes out any *other* in-progress/`monitoring.active` turn-level record whose `state.yaml` has independently gone terminal, regardless of session_id — belt-and-suspenders in case a future duplicate slips past the open-time fix anyway. It only closes pre-existing genuinely-terminal records and never creates one, so the "no eval opened → no-op" rule stays intact for sessions that never opened one.

**Cleanup:** confirmed field-by-field before deleting — `eval-20260827T161845-1TYTWV.json` had 0 subagents, `status: in-progress`, and the fabricated `session-<timestamp>` id; `eval-20260827T162201-YWMW6Z.json` (untouched) has 2 subagents, `status: success`, and the real `2026-08-25T17:14:37.010916Z` session id. Deleted only the orphan.

Also noticed a large set of other files now showing modified (`data/*-unified.json`, `workflows/boot/steps/*`, `workflows/morning-briefing/*`, `memory/working/morning-briefing-*.md`, `systems/boot-instrumentation/*`) — consistent with the real concurrent boot/morning-briefing session you described. Not touching any of those.

All hook files compile; `settings.json` untouched this round (still valid). `evolutions/.pending-changes.json` updated with this round's findings under the same `work-20260826-193329-eval-hook-lifecycle` item.
